about: docs/LAB_DIAGNOSIS.md as data. Each rule matches facts in ONE report and proposes a fix the person runs. The doctor never runs these. 'when' is all-of; ops: equals, not_equals, in, contains, not_contains, status, gt. 'who' is 'you' (no admin) or 'admin'. A null command means there is nothing to run, only something to know.

rules.title: No Python on this machine is new enough to run GINI
rules.reason: GINI and the doctor both need Python {stage0.min_python} or newer; every interpreter Stage 0 found is older, or does not run.

command.macos: brew install python@3.12    (or the installer from python.org)
command.linux: sudo apt install python3 python3-venv pipx    (Debian/Ubuntu; use your distribution's package manager otherwise)

rules.side_effects: Installs a new Python alongside any existing one; nothing is replaced.

rules.title: No container engine is installed
rules.reason: Every GINI element runs in a container; with neither Docker nor Podman there is nothing for gBuilder to start.

command.macos: Install Docker Desktop from docker.com, start it once, and allow it 6-8 GB of memory.
command.windows: Install Docker Desktop from docker.com (WSL 2 backend), start it once, and allow it 6-8 GB of memory.
command.linux: sudo apt install podman    (or Docker Engine from docs.docker.com)

rules.side_effects: Docker Desktop reserves the memory you give its VM whenever it is running.

rules.title: Docker is installed but its engine is not answering
rules.reason: docker info failed: {engine.docker.info}. gBuilder prefers Docker whenever the binary exists, so a stopped daemon blocks everything even if Podman would work.

command.macos: Start Docker Desktop and wait for it to say it is running.
command.windows: Start Docker Desktop and wait for it to say it is running.
command.linux: sudo systemctl start docker    (or set GINI_ENGINE=podman to use Podman instead)

rules.side_effects: None beyond the engine starting.

rules.title: Podman's storage uses an old user-id mapping
rules.reason: /etc/subuid grants {engine.podman.idmap.subuid}, but Podman's storage was created with {engine.podman.idmap.inuse}. Everything looks fine until an image needs a high uid, and then pulls fail with 'insufficient UIDs or GIDs available in user namespace'. The range is fine; the storage is stale.
rules.side_effects: Stops every running Podman container for your user, including an open GINI lab. Images are kept.

rules.title: This account has no subordinate user ids, so rootless Podman cannot start containers
rules.reason: Rootless Podman maps container users onto a range from /etc/subuid and /etc/subgid; without an entry every container fails at start. Different ranges on different machines are normal, a missing one is not.
rules.side_effects: podman system migrate stops your running Podman containers.

rules.title: No user runtime directory (usually an ssh login without a systemd user session)
rules.reason: Podman keeps its socket and auth file under XDG_RUNTIME_DIR; without it, behaviour changes with how you logged in.

command.linux: sudo loginctl enable-linger "$USER"    then log out and back in

rules.side_effects: Your user services keep running after you log out.

rules.title: Lingering is off, so your containers are killed when you log out
rules.reason: Without lingering systemd tears down the user session, and every container in it, at logout.
rules.side_effects: Your user services keep running after you log out.

rules.title: CPU limits cannot be applied to your containers
rules.reason: The cpu controller is not delegated to your user slice ({rootless.cgroup2.user.controllers}), so a sized GINI element's CPU cap has nowhere to go.

command.linux: sudo mkdir -p /etc/systemd/system/user@.service.d && printf '[Service]\nDelegate=cpu cpuset io memory pids\n' | sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/user@.service.d/delegate.conf && sudo systemctl daemon-reload    then log out and back in

rules.side_effects: Applies to every user on the machine.

rules.title: Podman is using the slow vfs storage driver
rules.reason: vfs copies every layer in full: far slower and much larger on disk than overlay. It usually means fuse-overlayfs is missing ({rootless.tool.fuse-overlayfs}).

command.linux: sudo apt install fuse-overlayfs    then: podman system reset

rules.side_effects: podman system reset DELETES all your Podman images, containers and volumes; they are re-pulled on next use.

rules.title: A stored registry credential is blocking image pulls
rules.reason: The registry answers anonymously, but {engine.gini.engine.effective} is refused when it uses its stored login: {registry.engine}. On shared home directories this breaks every machine at once.
rules.side_effects: Pulls become anonymous; any private registry you use will need docker login again.

rules.title: The image registry cannot be reached from this machine
rules.reason: An anonymous request to Docker Hub failed: {registry.anonymous}. That is network, proxy or TLS, not GINI.

rules.title: gBuilder is not installed for this user
rules.reason: No gbuilder launcher or pipx environment for gini-toolkit was found.
rules.side_effects: Installs gBuilder into its own environment; nothing else changes.

rules.title: Qt (PySide6) does not import in gBuilder's Python
rules.reason: Importing PySide6 failed: {qt.pyside6}. gBuilder cannot open a window until it does.
rules.side_effects: Rebuilds gBuilder's environment; your projects and settings are not touched.

rules.title: A library Qt needs to draw windows is missing (libxcb-cursor)
rules.reason: Without libxcb-cursor gBuilder will not start at all, and the error names a Qt platform plugin rather than a package.
rules.side_effects: None.

rules.title: The CPU governor is 'powersave', the most likely cause of a stuttering Machine Lab feed
rules.reason: xv6 is emulated in software on one core; a governor that keeps deciding the load is not worth ramping up for produces a feed that is fine and then is not.

command.linux: sudo cpupower frequency-set -g performance    (or your distribution's tuned profile)

rules.side_effects: More power use and heat while the machine is busy.

rules.title: The CPU has been thermally throttled
rules.reason: The kernel counted {perf.cpu.throttle.count} throttling events. That is proof, not a theory, and nothing in GINI can fix it.

rules.title: Your user session has a hard CPU cap
rules.reason: The user slice is limited to {perf.cgroup.user.cpu_max}; a container inside it cannot exceed that however its own limits are written.

rules.title: The compose provider cannot exec into its own service (fine for current GINI)
rules.reason: Running a command in the container works the way gBuilder does it; only the compose provider's route fails. This explains older failures and needs no fix.

rules.title: gini-grouter has been downloaded but not under the name GINI runs (gini-grouter:latest)
rules.reason: GINI resolves gini-grouter:latest; this machine only has registry tags ({gini.image.gini-grouter}). Every topology using this element fails at Run until the plain tag exists.
rules.side_effects: Adds a tag; nothing is downloaded or removed.

rules.title: gini-grouter:latest is listed but does not resolve (the engine's tag index lost it)
rules.reason: {gini.image.gini-grouter.runtime}. Docker Desktop has been seen doing this straight after a pull and re-tag; gBuilder repairs it when Run asks for the image, and this command does the same by hand.
rules.side_effects: Re-applies an existing tag; nothing is downloaded or removed.
